title: Define behavior & UX spec
body:
## Overview
Establish the complete behavioral and UX specification for the Homepage Hero CTA section before any implementation begins.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Document all CTA button states: default, hover, active, disabled, loading
- [ ] Define scroll behavior trigger points and animation curves
- [ ] Specify responsive breakpoints (mobile 320px, tablet 768px, desktop 1280px+)
- [ ] Include annotated wireframes or Figma link covering all states
- [ ] Review sign-off from design lead and product owner

## Notes
This spec gates all other Hero issues. Must be merged to `main` before work begins on HERO-002 through HERO-007.

title: Smooth scroll
body:
## Overview
Implement smooth, physics-based scroll behavior when the Hero CTA button is clicked and targets an anchor section below the fold.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Clicking the CTA scrolls to the `#features` section smoothly (no instant jump)
- [ ] Scroll duration: 600ms with ease-in-out easing
- [ ] Works across Chrome, Firefox, Safari, and Edge (latest 2 versions)
- [ ] Respects `prefers-reduced-motion` — falls back to instant scroll
- [ ] No layout shift or paint during scroll animation

## Implementation Notes
Use `window.scrollTo({ behavior: 'smooth' })` with a polyfill for Safari. Guard with `matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)')` check.

## Related
Depends on HERO-001 (UX spec) for target anchor definition.

title: Demo scenario loader
body:
## Overview
Build a lightweight scenario loader that populates the Hero section with pre-defined demo content (copy, imagery, CTA label) based on a URL query parameter or user segment.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Supports `?scenario=startup`, `?scenario=enterprise`, `?scenario=agency` query params
- [ ] Each scenario loads its own headline, subheadline, CTA label, and background image
- [ ] Falls back to default Hero content when no param is present or param is invalid
- [ ] Scenario config stored in a single `hero-scenarios.json` file (not hardcoded)
- [ ] No visible flash of default content before scenario content renders

## Implementation Notes
Fetch scenario config on `DOMContentLoaded`. Apply before first paint using inline `<script>` in `<head>` or SSR pre-rendering.

title: Loading state & debounce
body:
## Overview
Add a visual loading state to the Hero CTA button and debounce rapid repeated clicks to prevent duplicate API calls or navigation events.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Button shows a spinner icon and 'Loading…' label within 100ms of click
- [ ] Button is disabled (pointer-events: none) during loading state
- [ ] Debounce threshold: 300ms — subsequent clicks within threshold are ignored
- [ ] Loading state resolves (success or error) and button returns to normal within 5s max
- [ ] ARIA: `aria-busy='true'` set on button during loading; `aria-live` region announces completion

## Related
Coordinates with HERO-006 (Keyboard accessibility & ARIA) for ARIA attribute contract.

title: Track click analytics
body:
## Overview
Instrument the Hero CTA button with click event tracking to capture user engagement data in the analytics platform.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Fires a `hero_cta_clicked` event on every button click
- [ ] Event payload includes: `{ timestamp, scenario, user_segment, page_variant, session_id }`
- [ ] Works with Google Analytics 4 (gtag) and the internal event bus
- [ ] Does not block or delay the primary click action
- [ ] No PII captured in the event payload
- [ ] Verified in GA4 DebugView and browser console before merge

## Implementation Notes
Use `navigator.sendBeacon` for non-blocking delivery. Wrap in try/catch so analytics failure never breaks the CTA.

title: Keyboard accessibility & ARIA
body:
## Overview
Ensure the Hero CTA button and surrounding section are fully keyboard-navigable and screen-reader-friendly per WCAG 2.1 AA.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] CTA button is reachable via Tab key from page top
- [ ] Enter and Space keys trigger the CTA action
- [ ] `role='button'` and `aria-label` set correctly on custom elements (native `<button>` preferred)
- [ ] Section heading has `aria-labelledby` pointing to Hero `<h1>`
- [ ] `aria-live='polite'` region announces CTA outcome (scroll start, loading, success)
- [ ] Passes automated axe-core scan with zero critical violations
- [ ] Manual test with NVDA + Chrome and VoiceOver + Safari documented

## Related
ARIA attribute contract shared with HERO-004 (Loading state & debounce).

title: Focus ring styling
body:
## Overview
Apply a visible, on-brand focus ring to the Hero CTA button that satisfies WCAG 2.1 AA contrast requirements.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Focus ring visible on keyboard focus (not mouse click) using `:focus-visible`
- [x] Ring color passes 3:1 contrast ratio against all Hero background variants
- [x] Offset: 3px; width: 2px; style: solid (or equivalent box-shadow approach)
- [x] Does not appear on mouse or touch interaction (`:focus-visible` selector only)
- [x] Reviewed in high-contrast Windows mode

## Implementation Notes
Use `outline: 2px solid var(--color-focus-ring); outline-offset: 3px;` scoped to `:focus-visible`. Confirmed shipped and passing QA.
